title: Making plans with friends
goal: Ask a friend if they're free, suggest what to do, agree where and when to meet, say you're on your way or running late, and cancel without upsetting anyone.
intro:
Welcome to **Part 2**. From here on the course is about real life: the Gujarati you need with friends, around town and at work. This unit is about making plans, which in Gujarati means a lot of **ચાલો** 'come on, let's', a lot of English words (**ફ્રી**, **બિઝી**, **પ્લાન**, **ટાઇમ**) and the famous **બસ, પાંચ મિનિટ!** 'just five minutes!'

You'll learn the everyday way to say 'let's' (**ચાલો, ફિલ્મ જોઈએ**) and 'shall we?' (**ક્યાં મળીએ?**), the friendly ways of telling friends what to do (**ટાઇમ પર આવજે!**, **મોડો ના પડતો!**), and how to say you're about to leave, on your way, or stuck in traffic.

grammar.title: Let's… and shall we…?: આપણે … -ઈએ
grammar.body:
To suggest doing something together, Gujarati uses the **subjunctive 'we' form** (stem + **-ઈએ**, unit 18), usually opened with **ચાલો** (to a group) or **ચાલ** (to one close friend):

**ચાલો, ફિલ્મ જોઈએ** 'let's watch a film' · **ચાલ, ચા પીએ** 'come on, let's have tea'

**Shall we?** — the same form as a question: **જઈએ?** 'shall we go?', **ક્યાં મળીએ?** 'where shall we meet?', **શું કરીએ?** 'what shall we do?'

**What if we…?** — add **તો** at the end. This is the most Gujarati way to float an idea: **આપણે ડુમસ જઈએ તો?** 'what if we went to Dumas?'

**Coaxing** — add **ને**: **ચાલ ને!** 'oh come on!', **જઈએ ને!** 'let's go, come on!'

The pronoun is **આપણે** 'we (you and I)', never **અમે** 'we (not you)': **આપણે** જઈએ? is a suggestion to your friend; **અમે** જઈએ? asks permission for you and your group to go.

The second trap: the future is not a suggestion. **આપણે કાલે મળીશું** states a plan ('we will meet tomorrow'); to propose it, say **કાલે મળીએ?**

examples.en: Shall we go to the mall tomorrow?
What shall we do on Saturday?

grammar.title: Telling friends what to do: આવ, આવજે, આવતો નહીં
grammar.body:
You met the three imperative levels in unit 11. With friends you'll use the **તું** forms all the time:

**Now: the bare stem** — **આવ** 'come', **બોલ** 'say', **જો** 'look', **ચાલ** 'come on'. Your default with close friends (with anyone else it sounds rude).
**Later: stem + -જે** — **આવજે**, **ફોન કરજે**, **કહેજે**. For things to do later, and it sounds a little softer: **ઘરે પહોંચીને મેસેજ કરજે** 'text me when you get home'.
**Don't (now)**: **ના** + stem: **ના જા** 'don't go', **વચ્ચે ના બોલ** 'don't interrupt'.
**Don't (later), as a warning**: the **-તો / -તી + નહીં** form, agreeing with the person: **ભૂલતો નહીં** 'don't forget' (to a man), **ભૂલતી નહીં** (to a woman). With ના in front it is just as common: **મોડો ના પડતો!** 'don't be late!'

**Softening**: add **ને** (આવ **ને**! 'do come!') or use a compound verb: **આવી જા** 'come on over' is friendlier than a bare આવ.

With a group, or with your friend's parents, switch to **-ઓ / -જો / -તા નહીં**: **આવો**, **આવજો**, **ભૂલતા નહીં**.

examples.en: Text me when you get home.
Don't be late tomorrow! (to a man)
Don't forget the key. (to a woman)
Come on over, it'll be fun!

grammar.title: About to leave, on the way, already there
grammar.body:
Being late is something of a national sport, so Gujarati has precise ways to say where you are in the process:

**About to**: **-વાનો / -વાની / -વાનાં + છે** (unit 17): **હું નીકળવાનો છું** 'I'm about to leave'.
**Just leaving**: the plain present + **જ**: **નીકળું જ છું** 'I'm just leaving'.
**On the way**: **રસ્તામાં છું** or the continuous **આવી રહ્યો છું** 'I'm coming'.
**Done**: stem + **-ઈ ગયો / ગઈ** (+ છું): **હું નીકળી ગયો છું** 'I've left', **હું પહોંચી ગઈ** 'I'm here'. The compound with જવું marks the change as complete.
**Promising**: **હું આવું છું** (simple present) also means 'I'm coming, I'll be right there': ઊભો રહે, **આવું છું**.

Everything agrees with the speaker: a woman says નીકળવા**ની** છું, નીકળી **ગઈ** છું, આવી **રહી** છું.

The trap: **હું નીકળ્યો** on its own sounds like a story ('I left'); for 'I've left (and I'm coming)' say **નીકળી ગયો છું**.

examples.en: We're leaving in half an hour.

examples.en: I'm getting ready, I'm just about to leave.

culture: Plans among friends in Gujarat are loose and made late — 'tonight?' at 5 pm is normal, and the WhatsApp group decides more than any one person. Almost every plan involves food: late-night snacks at Manek Chowk in Ahmedabad, bhajiya on Dumas beach or a Surati locho breakfast in Surat, the food stalls of Law Garden, or just a **કીટલી** (tea stall) where friends can sit for hours over a ₹10 cutting chai. Time is stretchy: **બસ, પાંચ મિનિટ** and **નીકળી ગયો છું** are often said by someone still at home, and twenty minutes' delay shocks nobody (offices, trains and weddings with a muhurat are another matter). A flat **ના** sounds harsh, so people soften it: **જોઈશું** 'we'll see', **નહીં ફાવે** 'it won't work out', **બીજા કોઈ દિવસે** 'another day'. With friends you use **તું**, but if a friend's parent picks up the phone, switch instantly to **તમે**, **જી** and a **જય શ્રી કૃષ્ણ** or **નમસ્તે, આન્ટી**. Goodbye among friends is **ચાલ, આવજે** — literally 'OK, do come again'.

tip.title: With friends: તું, and English words with Gujarati grammar
tip.body:
- With friends use **તું** and its verb: તું ફ્રી **છે**? (not છો).
- English adjectives just take છે: હું **બિઝી છું**, એ **ફ્રી છે**.
- English nouns get a Gujarati verb: પ્લાન **બનાવવો**.
- The Gujarati word **નવરો / નવરી** agrees like any adjective.

tip.title: Let's: ચાલો, … -ઈએ
tip.body:
- 'Let's' is the **-ઈએ** form: ચાલો, ફિલ્મ **જોઈએ**. To one close friend: **ચાલ**.
- As a question it means 'shall we?': **જઈએ?** ક્યાં **મળીએ?**
- Float an idea with **… -ઈએ તો?** 'what if we…?'
- Say **આપણે** (you and me), not **અમે** (us, not you).

tip.title: Telling friends what to do
tip.body:
- Now: bare stem — **આવ**, **જો**, **ચાલ**. Later: **-જે** — **આવજે**, **ફોન કરજે**.
- Don't (now): **ના** + stem: **ના જા**.
- Don't (warning): **-તો / -તી નહીં** — **ભૂલતો નહીં** (to a man), **ભૂલતી નહીં** (to a woman); also **મોડો ના પડતો!**
- To a group or to elders: **આવો, આવજો, ભૂલતા નહીં**.

tip.title: About to leave → on the way → there
tip.body:
- About to: **નીકળવાનો / નીકળવાની છું**. Just leaving: **નીકળું જ છું**.
- On the way: **રસ્તામાં છું**, **આવી રહ્યો / રહી છું**.
- Done: **નીકળી ગયો / ગઈ છું**, **પહોંચી ગઈ**.
- 'Coming!' is the plain present: **આવું છું!**
- All of it agrees with the speaker.
tip.pattern: નીકળવાનો છું → રસ્તામાં છું → પહોંચી ગયો

sentences.en: I'm leaving in ten minutes. (man)
I'm just leaving.

sentences.native: હું આવી રહી છું, રસ્તામાં છું.
sentences.roman: huṃ āvī rahī chhuṃ, rastāmāṃ chhuṃ.
sentences.en: I'm coming, I'm on the way. (woman)

sentences.native: નેહા નીકળી ગઈ છે, પંદર મિનિટમાં પહોંચશે.
sentences.roman: nehā nīkaḷī gaī chhe, pandar miniṭmāṃ pahoṃchshe.
sentences.en: Neha has left, she'll be there in fifteen minutes.

sentences.native: અમે પહોંચી ગયા, તું ક્યાં છે?
sentences.roman: ame pahoṃchī gayā, tuṃ kyāṃ chhe?
sentences.en: We're here, where are you?

sentences.native: રિલીફ રોડ પર બહુ ટ્રાફિક છે, હું ફસાઈ ગયો.
sentences.roman: rilīf roḍ par bahu ṭrāfik chhe, huṃ fasāī gayo.
sentences.en: There's loads of traffic on Relief Road, I'm stuck.

sentences.native: બસ, પાંચ મિનિટ! હું રસ્તામાં છું.
sentences.roman: bas, pāṃch miniṭ! huṃ rastāmāṃ chhuṃ.
sentences.en: Just five minutes! I'm on my way.

sentences.native: હું અડધા કલાકથી તારી વાટ જોઉં છું!
sentences.roman: huṃ aḍdhā kalākthī tārī vāṭ jouṃ chhuṃ!
sentences.en: I've been waiting for you for half an hour!
Late again today?

sentences.native: મને થોડું લેટ થશે, તમે જમવાનું શરૂ કરો.
sentences.roman: mane thoḍuṃ leṭ thashe, tame jamvānuṃ sharū karo.
sentences.en: I'll be a bit late, you all start eating.
Wait, I'm coming!

tip.title: Saying no without saying no
tip.body:
- A bare **ના** sounds harsh. Say **નહીં ફાવે** 'it won't work out', give a reason, and offer another day: **બીજા કોઈ દિવસે રાખીએ?**
- **જોઈશું** 'we'll see' often means no.
- **કૅન્સલ કરવું** = you cancel it (ergative: મેં ટિકિટ કૅન્સલ **કરી**); **કૅન્સલ થવું** = it got cancelled: શો કૅન્સલ **થઈ ગયો**.

sentences.native: સૉરી યાર, આજે નહીં ફાવે, ઘરે મહેમાન છે.
sentences.roman: sorī yār, āje nahīṃ fāve, ghare mahemān chhe.
sentences.en: Sorry, man, I can't make it today, we've got guests at home.
Today's plan is off, let's meet tomorrow.

sentences.native: વરસાદ આવ્યો એટલે શો કૅન્સલ થઈ ગયો.
sentences.roman: varsād āvyo eṭle sho kensal thaī gayo.
sentences.en: It rained, so the show got cancelled.
I cancelled the ticket.
Stop making excuses, tell the truth!

sentences.native: એની પાસે હંમેશાં કોઈ બહાનું હોય છે.
sentences.roman: enī pāse hammeshāṃ koī bahānuṃ hoy chhe.
sentences.en: He always has some excuse.

sentences.native: બીજા કોઈ દિવસે રાખીએ? શનિવારે ફાવશે?
sentences.roman: bījā koī divase rākhīe? shanivāre fāvshe?
sentences.en: Shall we make it another day? Does Saturday work?
We'll see. Give me a call.

sentences.native: કાલે નહીં ફાવે, પણ રવિવારે પાક્કું.
sentences.roman: kāle nahīṃ fāve, paṇ ravivāre pākkuṃ.
sentences.en: Tomorrow won't work, but Sunday for sure.

sentences.native: ખરેખર સૉરી, મારે ઑફિસમાં મોડે સુધી રોકાવું પડશે.
sentences.roman: kharekhar sorī, māre ofismāṃ moḍe sudhī rokāvuṃ paḍshe.
sentences.en: Really sorry, I'll have to stay late at the office.
